name: github.auth.status
description: Preflight the GitHub CLI surface: whether a GitHub CLI is present on this execution lane (`available`) and whether it holds usable credentials there (`authenticated`). Neither absence nor a missing credential is an error. Quota fields and detail: the orbit skill's tool-surface.md reference, section `GitHub auth status`.

name: github.pr.list
description: List pull requests with their current head SHAs. Defaults to open pull requests.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Pull-request state filter: open (default), closed, merged, or all

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: Restrict to pull requests targeting one base branch

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum pull requests to return (default 30, capped at 100)

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository in owner/name format (uses current directory if omitted)

name: github.run.list
description: List recent GitHub Actions workflow runs with each run's reported head SHA. Filter by branch, workflow, status/conclusion, and event.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Restrict to runs for one branch

parameters.name: workflow
parameters.description: Restrict to one workflow file name (for example codeql.yml) or numeric workflow id; a job display name is not a workflow name and is not accepted

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Restrict to one run status or conclusion (queued, in_progress, completed, failure, success, cancelled, timed_out, action_required)

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Restrict to one triggering event (push, pull_request, schedule)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum runs to return (default 20, capped at 100)

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository in owner/name format (uses current directory if omitted)

name: github.run.logs
description: Read a bounded excerpt of one GitHub Actions run's logs — failed steps by default, or the full log — plus runner checkout evidence. Source limits, step mapping and job-log recovery: the orbit skill's tool-surface.md reference, section `GitHub run logs`.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: Numeric job ID to narrow the log to one job

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: "failed" (default) for failed-step logs, or "all" for the full run log — use "all" to evidence the checked-out commit, since the checkout step usually succeeds

parameters.name: max_bytes
parameters.description: Maximum head/tail excerpt bytes (default 16384, capped at 262144), plus omission markers and up to 64 KiB of nextest failure blocks (16 KiB per block, at most 128 blocks). failure_regions includes original byte ranges; selection_complete is false if the scan or block-count limit is reached. The separate complete diagnostic_unit is capped at 262144 bytes.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository in owner/name format (uses current directory if omitted)

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: Exact workflow step name to return only that step's log section (usually with job); fails if absent. A workflow `name:` differing from the raw-log `Run <command>` cannot be mapped: omit `step` and pass `job` with `scope` or a byte/line window.

parameters.name: byte_start
parameters.description: Start of a byte window (0-based, inclusive); with byte_end returns exactly those bytes, bounded by max_bytes

parameters.name: byte_end
parameters.description: End of a byte window (0-based, exclusive); must be greater than byte_start

parameters.name: line_start
parameters.description: Start of a line window (1-based, inclusive); with line_end returns exactly those lines, bounded by max_bytes

parameters.name: line_end
parameters.description: End of a line window (1-based, exclusive); must be greater than line_start

name: github.run.view
description: Inspect one GitHub Actions workflow run: its reported head SHA, event, branch, and every job with its URL, steps, and conclusions. Unsuccessful jobs and steps are also collected separately.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository in owner/name format (uses current directory if omitted)

name: orbit.agents.ci_failures
description: Required-check failures on candidate heads, one record per head and check with the task, the run that produced the head, the check, its error signature and its cause class (code, flaky, infrastructure or unknown), newest first, with per-class counts. Each record lists the audited class changes later evidence made. Filter by window, task and class.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Failures first recorded in this period ending at until: all, or a duration such as 14d (units m, h, d or w). Default: 30d.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: End the window at this RFC 3339 instant, or this long ago (for example 7d). Omitted, the window ends now. A future instant is refused.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Only failures whose current class is this: code (the head's own change), flaky (the same head passed on a rerun), infrastructure (a declared infrastructure signature, the runner or network, or a base that fails the same check) or unknown (no cause established).

name: orbit.agents.scorecard
description: Rank one agent role's models by recorded reasoning effort over the window by weighted outcome rate per 100 units of work. `by_type` and `per_task` switch the output. Scoring rules, switches and cost: the orbit skill's references/tool-surface.md, section `Agent scorecards`.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: The agent role to score: implementers, reviewers or pilots.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Counts work in this period ending now: 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d or all (served as 90d, the scan's reach), or over the newest delivery attempts the scan holds: last50, last200, last500 or last1000. Default: 30d.

parameters.name: min_support
parameters.description: Units of the role's work a row needs before it is ranked, at least 1; rows below it are listed last without a rank. Default: 10.

parameters.name: execution
parameters.description: Which tasks implementer counts read, by how each was executed (derived from its runs): managed (a job worked its final implementation attempt), all (managed and interactive) or interactive (reached review or done in an interactive session, without a job) as a separate series. Tasks neither yet are in none. Cost and run time count managed tasks whatever this says. Other roles ignore it. Default: managed.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: End the window at this RFC 3339 instant, or this long ago (for example 30d; units m, h, d or w). The window is then [until - window, until). A count window (last50 and the other lastN values) takes the newest that many attempts before until. Omitted, the window ends now. A future instant is refused. Reviewer provisional counts stay measured against now.

parameters.name: by_type
parameters.description: Split implementers into (crew, model, tier, type) cells using workflow.task_types, with two-level shrinkage; implementers only.

parameters.name: per_task
parameters.description: Export one row per implemented task for offline analysis, with its crew, model, tier, configured type, tags, context-file path prefixes and per-term counts; implementers only, and not with by_type.

name: orbit.agents.show
description: One row of an agent role's scorecard and, for each term, its count, rate and contribution with the task IDs behind the count and the records that make it. Use it to follow a count from `orbit.agents.scorecard` to its tasks. Scans the workspace once per call (cache_ttl_seconds 0).

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: The agent role to score: implementers, reviewers or pilots.

parameters.name: row_effort
parameters.description: The row's recorded reasoning effort (low, medium, high, xhigh or max), provider_default for a null effort, or unknown for work with no recorded effort; optional when the crew and model name one row.

parameters.name: row_model
parameters.description: The row's model (`model unknown` for runs that recorded none); optional when the crew has one row.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Counts work in this period ending now: 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d or all (served as 90d, the scan's reach), or over the newest delivery attempts the scan holds: last50, last200, last500 or last1000. Default: 30d.

parameters.name: min_support
parameters.description: Units of the role's work a row needs before it is ranked, at least 1; rows below it are listed last without a rank. Default: 10.

parameters.name: execution
parameters.description: Which tasks implementer counts read, by how each was executed (derived from its runs): managed (a job worked its final implementation attempt), all (managed and interactive) or interactive (reached review or done in an interactive session, without a job) as a separate series. Tasks neither yet are in none. Cost and run time count managed tasks whatever this says. Other roles ignore it. Default: managed.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: End the window at this RFC 3339 instant, or this long ago (for example 30d; units m, h, d or w). The window is then [until - window, until). A count window (last50 and the other lastN values) takes the newest that many attempts before until. Omitted, the window ends now. A future instant is refused. Reviewer provisional counts stay measured against now.

name: orbit.attention
description: List operator waits and suggested next actions; use at session start or on-call triage, checking degraded sources before treating an empty result as clear. Details: installed Orbit skill `references/attention.md`.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Registered workspace names or IDs, as one string or an array; conflicts with all.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Read every active workspace on this host.

name: orbit.auto_task
description: List, add, update or mint recurring auto-task definitions.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Action (required): list; add (name, schedule, template); update (name); mint (name).

parameters.name: granted_tools
parameters.description: add, update: Operator only; minted granted tools (empty clears on update, disallowed in `template`).

parameters.name: acknowledge_unconditional
parameters.description: mint: Unconditional mint ack; operator only.

name: orbit.automation.explain
description: Explain a routine's `trigger.condition`, an auto-task's `schedule.condition`, or `job:<name>` steps against live workspace state. Reports the scope, matches and closest misses, one subject's clause tree with operand values (unreadable values are unknown, never false), and durable tracking; job mode shows the steps checked at load. Read-only: it writes nothing, evaluates no waits and mints nothing; enabled jobs run detached and park while a step waits. Details: installed Orbit skill `references/tool-surface.md`, row `Condition explain`.

parameters.name: definition
parameters.description: The routine or auto-task carrying the condition: its name, or `routine:<name>` / `auto-task:<name>` when a routine and an auto-task share the name. `job:<name>` explains that job's auto-task steps instead.

name: orbit.codebase
description: Codebase analytics: ranked rollups, one key's detail, or files changed together.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: show: Rollup key (file/dir/crate); related: Repo-relative file.

parameters.name: rollup
parameters.description: show, analytics: file (default), dir, or crate.

name: orbit.command.exec
description: Execute a command as an explicit argv array in an explicit working directory and return its stdout, stderr, and exit status, within a deadline. Requires operator capability and the workspace claim; withheld from managed runs. The child receives an allowlisted environment: baseline process context, git author and committer identity, and Orbit's execution envelope.

parameters.name: argv
parameters.description: Argv JSON array (never a shell string).

name: orbit.decision
description: List, show or raise human decision requests.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Action (required): list; show (id); raise (task_id, question, options).

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: list: Task ID; raise: Open human-crew task ID.

parameters.name: topic
parameters.description: list: Exact topic; raise: Topic ID (1-64 `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]`).

name: orbit.decision.digest
description: Raise the approval decision requests a decision channel's digest presents, and return the whole digest in one call. Callable only by the plugin the channel is bound to, through its callback session, or by the operator, never by an agent session. Repeated calls reuse requests for unchanged task bindings; newly eligible tasks can add requests. With the decision channel disabled, it returns no requests. The binding rules and result fields are in the orbit skill's references/tool-surface.md, section `Decision requests`.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The registered decision channel the digest is for, as `orbit decision channel list` shows it.

name: orbit.decision.submit
description: Submit a human's answer to one open decision request through a registered decision channel. Callable only by the plugin the channel is bound to, through its callback session, or by the operator testing the channel, never by an agent session. Core verifies the channel, the request's binding, the answer and the single-use token, and checks a forwarded raw message's DKIM signature itself. A refusal returns its error code and applies nothing. The refusal codes, DKIM rules and retry behaviour are in the orbit skill's references/tool-surface.md, section `Decision requests`.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The registered decision channel submitting the answer, as `orbit decision channel list` shows it.

parameters.name: answer
parameters.description: The human's chosen answer id, one of the request's allowed answers. An empty answer is refused as unparseable.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The per-request single-use token minted for this request under the channel key. Core verifies it; presenting it never reveals it back.

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: Evidence or note kept with the answer. A pilot-admission `evaluated` answer uses it as its evidence and is refused without one.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: The transport sender the submission presents as evidence. A plugin submission must present one; when the channel has a sender allowlist, the sender must be on it. The operator's own test submission may omit it.

parameters.name: auth_results
parameters.description: The raw Authentication-Results header the transport forwards as evidence. A plugin submission must forward one: core requires dkim=pass and spf=pass and refuses on dmarc=fail. The operator's own test submission may omit it.

parameters.name: raw_message
parameters.description: The raw reply message the transport forwards for core-side DKIM verification, at most 262144 bytes (256 KiB). When present, core verifies the message's DKIM signature itself and refuses when its result contradicts the forwarded verdicts. Required on a channel registered with require_dkim_verification; optional otherwise.

name: orbit.drain.claim.bind
description: Bind an executor's local leaf run to its execution claim on the owner, moving the claim from `claimed` to `running`. Idempotent: repeating the same run returns the recorded outcome, and a different run is refused, so one claim never has two leaves. The owner fences the claim against the session's own machine; a claim admitted to another machine, or already settled or revoked, is refused as stale.

parameters.name: claim_id
parameters.description: The claim `orbit.task.pull` admitted to this machine.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: The one local leaf run the executor created for this claim.

parameters.name: ship
parameters.description: The ship contract the claim was admitted under, from its receipt.

name: orbit.drain.claim.effort
description: Report, after the fact, the reasoning effort and implementing model a claimed leaf ran at when its settlement carried none. Attribution only; it changes no claim, task or run outcome. Who may call and the conflict refusals: the orbit skill's tool-surface.md reference, section `Distributed drain tools`.

parameters.name: claim_id
parameters.description: The settled claim whose leaf ran on this machine.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: The leaf run bound to that claim.

parameters.name: reasoning_effort
parameters.description: The effective reasoning effort of the leaf's main implementing invocation, read from this machine's own records: its name (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`), or `provider_default` when the provider's default applied. Never sent for an unknown effort.

parameters.name: crew_model
parameters.description: The model of that same implementing invocation (else of its latest matching launch record), read from this machine's own records. Omitted when unknown; never derived from a crew name or configuration.

parameters.name: crew
parameters.description: The crew the leaf run actually used, read from this machine's own run record. Sent with the same report as `crew_model`, so the owner keys the attempt to this crew and model together when the task was re-crewed between claims. Omitted when unknown; an owner that predates it ignores the field.

name: orbit.drain.claim.settle
description: Settle an execution claim on the owner. A typed handoff is accepted only after the owner reads the pull request from the provider and resolves its candidate and base in the owner's own checkout, and only with digest-pinned validation evidence; it moves the task to `review`, which awaits owner approval — it does not merge. A failure records its evidence and blocks the task. A release (a cancelled drain giving back work it will not finish) returns the task to the backlog with its reason as a comment. Each releases only this claim's reservation. Retries replay the recorded outcome.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: The leaf run bound to this claim, when one was bound.

parameters.name: settlement
parameters.description: The executor's durable settlement: `{"AcceptHandoff": <typed handoff>}` for a published pull request, `{"Fail": <evidence>}`, or `{"Release": <evidence>}` to hand an unfinished claim back. Nothing else settles a claim.

parameters.name: crew
parameters.description: Optional. The crew the leaf run resolved. Attribution only: the owner records it on the claim's settlement record, after any crew the settlement's own evidence names, and never uses it to validate or decide the settlement.

parameters.name: crew_model
parameters.description: Optional. The model the leaf's crew resolved to. Attribution only, like `crew`.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Optional. The branch the leaf run's worktree recorded. Attribution only, like `crew`; the owner shows it so an operator can inspect the run.

parameters.name: worktree_path
parameters.description: Optional. The absolute path of the leaf run's worktree on the executing machine. Attribution only, like `branch`.

parameters.name: reasoning_effort
parameters.description: Optional. The effective reasoning effort of the leaf's main implementing invocation: its name (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`), or `provider_default` when the provider's default applied. Omit it when the effort is unknown. Attribution only, like `crew`: the owner's agent scorecards count the attempt under it.

name: orbit.drain.claims
description: List this workspace's execution claims for inspection and deliberate recovery: phase, age, reservation expiry, execution machine, bound run, last recorded event, unresolved merge intent, and landing invalidation. Age, an expired reservation, and an absent local run are diagnostics, not proof that a worker died — nothing here reclaims, rebinds, or repairs a claim.

name: orbit.drain.probe
description: Read-only preflight for the distributed drain, served by the workspace owner. Reports the owner, version, protocol schema, held capabilities and ship configuration; creates no receipt, claim or task transition. Fields and caller_* inputs: the orbit skill's tool-surface.md reference, section `Distributed drain tools`.

parameters.name: caller_version
parameters.description: Optional. The calling binary's version. When supplied, the response reports whether it matches this owner instead of leaving the caller to compare.

parameters.name: caller_schema
parameters.description: Optional. The caller's distributed-drain wire-protocol schema version. This is not the MCP protocol revision and not the orchestration schema version.

parameters.name: caller_fingerprint
parameters.description: Optional. Type-derived pull request schema fingerprint. Discover the owner's protocol_fingerprint before declaring this field; a mismatch raises protocol_skew before any pull.

parameters.name: caller_before_pr
parameters.description: Optional. Whether the executor's `review.timing` is `before_pr`. Diagnostic only: a claimed leaf runs the before-PR review the owner's ship contract captures, never the executor's own. After-landing review never affects admission.

name: orbit.drain.receipt.lookup
description: Read-only reconciliation of one distributed-drain admission request, served by the workspace owner. Returns the original receipt and the current claim phase (`found`), a non-reusable tombstone (`expired`), or `not_found`. It creates no receipt, binds no run, and grants no execution authority: a receipt is historical evidence, and `not_found` is not proof that an earlier request cannot still arrive, so it never licenses a replacement request under a new ID.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The durable request ID the original admission was made with. It is read verbatim; the stored receipt is never rewritten to match the caller's current binary.

parameters.name: machine_id
parameters.description: Optional receipt namespace: the machine the original request was made from. Defaults to this session's own machine. Naming another machine is cross-attempt inspection and requires operator capability.

parameters.name: lookup_schema
parameters.description: Optional lookup protocol version; defaults to 1. Versioned independently of admission, so an upgraded client can reconcile an old request. An incompatible version is refused — reconcile through owner claim inspection instead of minting a replacement request.

name: orbit.evolution.add
description: Record an interactive cost event in the bound workspace. Signature events corroborate one non-terminal evolution record; unsigned costs are retained without creating a capability gap. Returns {event, record}. Does not create friction or propose work.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Cost event: kind (workaround, manual_step, retry, wait), what (one line), minutes, retries, slot_minutes (nonnegative integers), wished (required for workaround/manual_step), signature (optional kebab-case key, 3-64 characters).

parameters.name: mandate
parameters.description: Optional assignment task for this occurrence.

name: orbit.evolution.list
description: List evolution signatures in the bound workspace, sorted by summed minutes plus slot_minutes. Returns {count, records}; each includes occurrence_count, distinct_cycles, distinct_mandates, cycle_count, mandate_count, minutes, retries and slot_minutes derived over the requested window. Friction is excluded. Declined signatures become eligible when suppression expires or window cost doubles.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Filter open, proposed, declined or resolved; omitted returns all states.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: RFC 3339 lower bound for occurrence aggregates. Records without occurrences in the window are omitted.

name: orbit.evolution.show
description: Show one evolution record in the bound workspace, its occurrences, proposal state, suppression window and all-time aggregates. Friction identifiers are not accepted.

name: orbit.experiment.abandon
description: Abandon a draft, running or paused experiment without a conclusion. It enrolls no new tasks. A fresh admission applies no overlay from the abandoned experiment; runs and claims already admitted keep the treatment they captured. Operator only: an agent session is refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded on the experiment's event.

name: orbit.experiment.assign
description: Force a nonterminal task with no arm assignment, or with an explicit_crew exclusion for this experiment, into an active arm of a running experiment, shadow or live. Records forced=true. Existing arm assignments and exclusions other than that explicit_crew exclusion are refused; overlapping experiment surfaces are refused. Operator only: an agent session is refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

name: orbit.experiment.clone
description: Copy an experiment's definition (hypothesis, arms with their current weights and overlays, population, metrics, sample rules, mode) into a new draft under a new name and a fresh assignment salt. Retired arms are not copied. The source is unchanged. Operator only: an agent session is refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The new draft's name, unique among this workspace's experiments.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded on the experiment's event.

name: orbit.experiment.conclude
description: Conclude a running or paused experiment. Records the chosen arm (or none), the reason, and the readout JSON at that moment on the conclusion event, which orbit experiment show returns. A chosen arm files one proposed task naming the experiment, arm, readout verdict and overlay; no arm files nothing. Assignment stops. A fresh admission applies no overlay from the concluded experiment; runs and claims already admitted keep the treatment they captured. Changes no configuration or repository file. Operator only: an agent session is refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

parameters.name: arm
parameters.description: The arm chosen as the winner. Omit to conclude with no winner.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded on the experiment's event.

name: orbit.experiment.create
description: Define a new experiment in draft: its arms (one control plus treatments, each with a weight and an overlay), the tasks it enrolls, its primary metric, guardrails and sample rules. Arms and overlays are validated on write and each overlay's digest is recorded. A draft assigns nothing. Operator only: an agent session is refused.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: A name unique among this workspace's experiments.

parameters.name: hypothesis
parameters.description: What the experiment expects the treatment arms to change, and why.

parameters.name: arms
parameters.description: The arms as a JSON array, each {"name", "control", "weight", "overlay"}. Exactly one arm is the control; weights are positive integers (default 1). An overlay is an object with any of: instructions (role implement, review or recovery to a repository file path, or false to suppress the shipped default), skills ({"replace": {skill name: bundle directory}, "roles"}), tools ({"add", "remove", "roles"}), crew ({"pool": [{"crew", "weight"}]}), config ({"values": {key: value}, "roles"}) and memory ({"roles", "global"}: deliver the drawn crew's model memory, and the global memory when global is true, as data; experimental). Roles default to implement. Unknown fields are refused.

parameters.name: population
parameters.description: Which tasks the experiment enrolls, as a JSON object with any of: complexity, task_type, tags_include, tags_exclude and origin, each a list of strings. Empty enrolls every task.

parameters.name: primary_metric
parameters.description: The whole-task metric the verdict is read on: total_tokens, cost_usd, lead_time, first_pass_acceptance, review_repairs, step_recoveries, final_recoveries, failed_checks, merge_conflicts, delivery_done_rate, escaped_regressions, lines_changed, cost_per_line or lead_time_per_line. cost_per_line and lead_time_per_line divide arm totals by reviewable lines and require a lines_changed guardrail. Step-local metrics are exploratory and may be used as guardrails.

parameters.name: guardrails
parameters.description: Guardrail metrics as a JSON object from metric name to the threshold its difference from control may not pass, such as {"delivery_done_rate": "-5pt", "escaped_regressions": "+0"}.

parameters.name: min_sample
parameters.description: Tasks every arm needs before a verdict is given.

parameters.name: max_days
parameters.description: Days after start at which a verdict is given whatever the sample.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: shadow (default) records assignments without applying overlays; live experiments can start and resume, applying overlays on matching dispatches. Start requires base-admissible instruction files and skill bundles, registered enabled agent-facing added tools, and preservation of handoff tools; skill replacement currently supports Claude on Unix.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded on the experiment's event.

name: orbit.experiment.list
description: List the workspace's experiments, oldest first, with status, mode, current segment and arms. Filter by status. Read-only.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only experiments in this status: draft, running, paused, concluded or abandoned.

name: orbit.experiment.pause
description: Pause a running experiment: it enrolls no new tasks until resumed. Tasks already assigned keep their arm. Operator only: an agent session is refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded on the experiment's event.

name: orbit.experiment.readout
description: Compare experiment arms read-only: outcomes, intervals, differences, verdict. Computed now from its assignments and the records Orbit already keeps; `--metric` narrows the report while the verdict stays on the primary metric and guardrails. Estimator, exclusion and verdict details: https://orbit-cli.com/how-to/experiments/#read-the-readout.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Report only this metric; the verdict is still read on the primary metric and guardrails. One of implement_tokens, total_tokens, cost_usd, lead_time, implement_duration, turns_before_first_edit, result_bytes_before_first_edit, first_pass_acceptance, review_repairs, step_recoveries, final_recoveries, failed_checks, merge_conflicts, delivery_done_rate, escaped_regressions, lines_changed, cost_per_line or lead_time_per_line.

name: orbit.experiment.resume
description: Resume a paused experiment. Refused while 3 other experiments are already running. Operator only: an agent session is refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded on the experiment's event.

name: orbit.experiment.reweight
description: Change a running or paused experiment's arm weights, retire arms, or both. Each call opens a new segment, recorded in the event log with the weights before and after, so tasks assigned under different weights stay distinguishable. Operator only: an agent session is refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

parameters.name: weights
parameters.description: New weights as a JSON object from arm name to a positive integer. Arms not named keep their weight.

parameters.name: retire
parameters.description: Arms to retire: they take no new tasks. The control cannot be retired, and at least one treatment must remain.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded on the experiment's event.

name: orbit.experiment.show
description: Show one experiment: its definition, status and current segment, each arm with its weight, overlay and overlay digest, and every event in order with its actor, time and reason. Read-only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

name: orbit.experiment.start
description: Start a draft experiment, opening segment 1; from then on its definition is frozen. Refused unless experiments.enabled is true, while 3 experiments are already running, and unless the definition is complete: at least two arms with unique names, exactly one control, positive weights, a primary metric, and config overlays only for keys on experiments.config_keys. Operator only: an agent session is refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded on the experiment's event.

name: orbit.experiment.update
description: Edit a draft experiment's definition: name, hypothesis, arms (the given list replaces every arm), population, metrics and sample rules. Only a draft can be edited; a started experiment is refused and changes only through pause, resume, reweight, conclude or abandon, or is cloned into a new draft. Operator only: an agent session is refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The experiment's id or name, as `orbit.experiment.list` prints it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: A new name, unique among this workspace's experiments.

parameters.name: hypothesis
parameters.description: What the experiment expects the treatment arms to change, and why.

parameters.name: arms
parameters.description: The arms as a JSON array, each {"name", "control", "weight", "overlay"}. Exactly one arm is the control; weights are positive integers (default 1). An overlay is an object with any of: instructions (role implement, review or recovery to a repository file path, or false to suppress the shipped default), skills ({"replace": {skill name: bundle directory}, "roles"}), tools ({"add", "remove", "roles"}), crew ({"pool": [{"crew", "weight"}]}), config ({"values": {key: value}, "roles"}) and memory ({"roles", "global"}: deliver the drawn crew's model memory, and the global memory when global is true, as data; experimental). Roles default to implement. Unknown fields are refused.

parameters.name: population
parameters.description: Which tasks the experiment enrolls, as a JSON object with any of: complexity, task_type, tags_include, tags_exclude and origin, each a list of strings. Empty enrolls every task.

parameters.name: primary_metric
parameters.description: The whole-task metric the verdict is read on: total_tokens, cost_usd, lead_time, first_pass_acceptance, review_repairs, step_recoveries, final_recoveries, failed_checks, merge_conflicts, delivery_done_rate, escaped_regressions, lines_changed, cost_per_line or lead_time_per_line. cost_per_line and lead_time_per_line divide arm totals by reviewable lines and require a lines_changed guardrail. Step-local metrics are exploratory and may be used as guardrails.

parameters.name: guardrails
parameters.description: Guardrail metrics as a JSON object from metric name to the threshold its difference from control may not pass, such as {"delivery_done_rate": "-5pt", "escaped_regressions": "+0"}.

parameters.name: min_sample
parameters.description: Tasks every arm needs before a verdict is given.

parameters.name: max_days
parameters.description: Days after start at which a verdict is given whatever the sample.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: shadow (default) records assignments without applying overlays; live experiments can start and resume, applying overlays on matching dispatches. Start requires base-admissible instruction files and skill bundles, registered enabled agent-facing added tools, and preservation of handoff tools; skill replacement currently supports Claude on Unix.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded on the experiment's event.

name: orbit.friction
description: Record a friction, or update one.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: add: Markdown body; update: Replacement body.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: add: Handle (<= 120 chars, default from body); update: Replacement (<= 120 chars, empty resets).

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: add: Friction tags (string or array): automation | build | docs | history-diverged | lifecycle | naming | other | policy | skill-guidance | tooling; defaults to other; update: Replacement tags (string or array): automation | build | docs | history-diverged | lifecycle | naming | other | policy | skill-guidance | tooling.

parameters.name: rehome_to
parameters.description: update: Target workspace unless `move: false`; empty clears.

parameters.name: move
parameters.description: update: With `rehome_to`: false avoids moving (default true).

name: orbit.notice.close
description: Close a fleet notice by id or dedupe_key with a reason. The operator may close any notice; an orchestrator may close its own crew's notices and any orchestrator- or agent-authored notice; a managed agent, a resident cycle included, may close only its own task's notices. Closing a notice that is already closed or expired returns it unchanged with already_inactive: true.

parameters.name: dedupe_key
parameters.description: Close open notice holding this key in home workspace.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it never outranks the operator or a managed run's binding.

name: orbit.notice.list
description: List fleet notices, open ones unless status says otherwise. Output is {notices, degraded}; `degraded` names any owner that could not be read. Read-only. Scope and merge rules: the orbit skill's tool-surface.md reference, section `Fleet notices`.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: List notices across all workspaces on this owner (default selected only).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: State: open (default), closed, expired, or all.

parameters.name: include_global
parameters.description: Include global notices from other workspaces (default true).

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it never outranks the operator or a managed run's binding.

name: orbit.notice.post
description: Post a fleet notice: a short, scoped note every agent and operator in its scope should see until it stops being true. A repeated dedupe_key updates or corroborates the open one. Poster classes, expiry caps and refusals: the orbit skill's tool-surface.md reference, section `Fleet notices`.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: warn (the operator is needed: name the exact ask), incident (something is broken now), maintenance (planned work others should hold off or plan around) or info (anything else worth knowing).

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: One line, 1-120 characters, no control characters.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Plain text, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; Markdown is stored verbatim and never rendered as HTML.

parameters.name: dedupe_key
parameters.description: Subject key (1-128 chars `[a-z0-9._:/-]`); repeats update open notice.

parameters.name: linked_task
parameters.description: Linked task ID on this owner.

parameters.name: hosts
parameters.description: Up to 32 machine IDs (maintenance kind only).

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it never outranks the operator or a managed run's binding.

name: orbit.notice.show
description: Show one fleet notice in any effective state with its untruncated body; an operator also sees its history of posts, updates, corroborations and close. Read-only.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it never outranks the operator or a managed run's binding.

name: orbit.pipeline.invoke
description: Submit a durable pipeline run and return immediately with its run ID. Public submissions require an operator; managed runs may invoke only a host-authorized child pipeline admission.

name: orbit.pipeline.wait
description: Block until the supplied pipeline runs reach terminal state or timeout.

parameters.name: run_ids
parameters.description: One or more run IDs to wait for as a string or array of strings.

parameters.name: poll_interval_seconds
parameters.description: Optional poll cadence in seconds (default 5, clamped to a 1-second floor).

name: orbit.resident.checkpoint
description: Append one validated resident.checkpoint v1 JSON comment to the mandate's assignment task. Requires the mandate's live, unexpired cycle and matching run_id. Malformed records, stale cycles and a second checkpoint for the same cycle are refused without writes. Returns {task_id, checkpoint}. Observed authority in the record grants no rights.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: The mandate's assignment task: a task tagged `resident` carrying a resident/mandate.json artifact.

parameters.name: record
parameters.description: Complete resident.checkpoint v1 JSON object (kind, schema=1, mandate, cycle, run_id, crew, recovery_of, wake, authority, actions, decisions, requests, costs, notes, next_wake, continuity, outcome, probe). At most 64 KiB, 50 actions, 20 decisions, 20 costs and 600 note characters, where notes describe only this cycle's delta. Action keys are resident:<mandate>:<cycle>:<positive integer>.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it is recorded on a grant request as the relaying session and never grants authority.

name: orbit.resident.control
description: Control a resident mandate's firing: pause, resume, stop, wake (status_request makes the cycle checkpoint even when idle), takeover or release. Each action is a history entry with the caller and reason. Pause, stop and takeover start no new cycle; a live cycle keeps its frozen grant, checkpoints and exits at its boundary. Stop ends the mandate and moves the assignment to review once no cycle is live. Resume and release restore firing under the existing authority and never widen it. Any caller that can write the assignment may call it. Output {task_id, action, state, effective_at}.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: The mandate's assignment task: a task tagged `resident` carrying a resident/mandate.json artifact.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: pause (active to paused: no new cycle), resume (paused to active), stop (ends the mandate: no new cycle, then the assignment moves to review), wake (active: due on the next tick despite the heartbeat, never the cadence floor), takeover (active or paused to taken_over: no cycle fires) or release (taken_over to active).

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded in the assignment's history with the caller.

parameters.name: status_request
parameters.description: With wake: the cycle writes a checkpoint even when it has nothing else to do.

parameters.name: by_session
parameters.description: The session taking over or acting, recorded with the action.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it is recorded on a grant request as the relaying session and never grants authority.

name: orbit.resident.digest
description: Read the manager digest in the bound workspace: resident state, latest outcome, open requests and stalled flag; open escalations oldest first; reversible decisions in the window still awaiting veto; top evolution pains by minutes plus slot minutes with occurrence, cycle and mandate counts; evolution proposals awaiting human approval; and resident metrics totals. Read-only. Defaults to 14d and the top 5 pains.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start as a span (7d, 24h, 2w) or RFC 3339 instant; defaults to the configured evolution window.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it is recorded on a grant request as the relaying session and never grants authority.

name: orbit.resident.grant
description: Widen or narrow a resident mandate's authority: its rights (dispatch, promote, merge, plugin_upgrade) and covered workspaces. Narrowing applies at once; widening is the human's. Rules and output: the orbit skill's tool-surface.md reference, section `Resident tools`.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: The mandate's assignment task: a task tagged `resident` carrying a resident/mandate.json artifact.

parameters.name: add
parameters.description: Rights to add: dispatch, promote, merge or plugin_upgrade. Widening.

parameters.name: workspaces
parameters.description: Workspaces to add to the authority's scope; each must be one the mandate lists. Widening.

parameters.name: remove
parameters.description: Rights to remove. Narrowing: open to any caller that can write the assignment.

parameters.name: drop_workspaces
parameters.description: Workspaces to drop from the authority's scope. Narrowing.

parameters.name: deadline
parameters.description: A new RFC 3339 mandate deadline, earlier than the current one (or the first one). Narrowing: it rewrites the mandate's deadline. A later deadline is an ordinary mandate edit.

parameters.name: quote
parameters.description: The human's words authorizing a widening, verbatim (at most 2000 characters). Required when a caller without operator authority asks to widen: the grant request carries it to the human unchanged.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it is recorded on a grant request as the relaying session and never grants authority.

name: orbit.resident.list
description: List the workspace's resident mandates (tasks tagged resident): each with its state, goal, deadline, effective rights and workspaces, authority revision and open grant request count. Ended mandates only with include_ended. Read-only.

parameters.name: include_ended
parameters.description: Include mandates whose assignment is done, archived or rejected.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it is recorded on a grant request as the relaying session and never grants authority.

name: orbit.resident.metrics
description: Report the resident widening measures over a window, derived read-only from task history, decision requests, checkpoints and audit rows: interventions, escalation load, reversals and crash-recovery cost. Read-only. Measure definitions: the orbit skill's tool-surface.md reference, section `Resident tools`.

parameters.name: mandate
parameters.description: One mandate's assignment task. Without it, every resident mandate in the workspace is reported, with workspace totals.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start: a span such as 7d, 24h or 2w, or an RFC 3339 instant. Defaults to 30d.

parameters.name: baseline
parameters.description: An interactive orchestration assignment task for computing the same measures. Measures that cannot be derived from its history report not_derivable, never zero. Tasks in other workspaces are read via their owner; unreachable ones are listed in references.unreachable.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it is recorded on a grant request as the relaying session and never grants authority.

name: orbit.resident.relay
description: Relay a human's direction or answer to a resident mandate: writes one resident.answer comment carrying `quote` verbatim with `source` provenance, records your session as relayed_by, and wakes the resident. A relay never changes authority: input naming rights, workspaces, status or other fields is refused; widen through orbit.resident.grant. Refused for an empty or over-long quote (>4000 characters) or an ended mandate. Output {task_id, comment, answer}: comment is {index, at, by} (comments carry no ids) and answer is the record as written.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: The mandate's assignment task: a task tagged `resident` carrying a resident/mandate.json artifact.

parameters.name: quote
parameters.description: The human's words, verbatim (1-4000 characters). They reach the resident unchanged as a resident.answer comment; text that would need redaction (a secret or home path) is refused, never rewritten.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Where the words came from: {human, via, session?, said_at}. human names who said it, via the channel (chat, email, call), session the conversation it came from, said_at an RFC 3339 instant. No other fields.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The resident request or decision request this answers. A relayed answer is a direction: the human still answers the decision request itself.

parameters.name: reverses
parameters.description: The resident decision id this direction reverses.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it is recorded on a grant request as the relaying session and never grants authority.

name: orbit.resident.show
description: Show one resident mandate: the mandate artifact (or why it is missing or invalid), the effective authority (rights and the workspaces both the authority and the mandate cover), the authority record with its grant and narrowing history, open grant requests, the latest parsed checkpoint and live cycle, the status line (the mandate's one info notice: title, body, when it was posted and lapses, and stale once it has lapsed), and the mandate's state (active, handed_off, ended or invalid). Read-only.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: The mandate's assignment task: a task tagged `resident` carrying a resident/mandate.json artifact.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it is recorded on a grant request as the relaying session and never grants authority.

name: orbit.routine.control
description: List workspace routine status, toggle one definition using its observed enabled state and target, or replace its trigger using its observed trigger and target. Requires trusted operator authority and explicit workspace. Never replay a change after a lost reply; observe authoritative state first.

name: orbit.run
description: List, show, observe or resume workflow runs.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: list: Max runs (<=200, default 25); show: Page size.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: show, observe, resume: Job run ID.

parameters.name: source_repair
parameters.description: resume: {action:inspect|submit|reconcile,task_id,request_key?,binding?,diagnosis?,reservation_digest?,unmet_acceptance?,policy_digest?}; prior inspect + plan for submit/reconcile.

name: orbit.search
description: Search tasks and frictions using lexical matching. With `kind: friction` and no `query`, list friction records instead: every status unless a `friction:` status narrows it, filtered by `tag`, ordered by creation time then ID, each hit carrying the full `record`; a note reports a listing cut at `limit`.

parameters.name: all_workspaces
parameters.description: All active workspaces (not in managed runs).

name: orbit.task.add
description: Create a task and return its JSON; rules are in the installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

name: orbit.task.artifact
description: Read/attach artifacts; list via `orbit.task.show` (`fields: ["artifacts"]`).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: get: Path from `orbit.task.show` (`field: "artifacts"`); put: Target path (default filename); `review-*` reserved except `review-report.json`.

parameters.name: source_path
parameters.description: put: Workspace file path (e.g. `.orbit/tmp/...`); escapes/`/tmp` rejected.

name: orbit.task.block_triage
description: Triage proposed tasks a task-pilot warning holds. `candidates` lists held tasks; `propose` opens an operator decision; `report` records a human action. Policy and the proof recipe: the orbit skill's references/tool-surface.md, section `Pilot-warning triage`.

name: orbit.task.eligible
description: List backlog and proposed tasks that can be picked up now without colliding with work in flight, as {tasks, total, truncated[, conflicting]}. A task is eligible when its context-file lock surface overlaps no in-progress or review task's surface, decided by the same lock code automatic dispatch uses. No other gate applies: dependencies, complexity, groups, crew and overlap between candidates are not checked. Read-only.

name: orbit.task.list
description: List tasks as {tasks, total, truncated}; rules are in the installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Name fields, or fetch one task with `orbit.task.show`; compact rows match `orbit tool run orbit.task.list`.

name: orbit.task.pull
description: Distributed-drain admission, served by the workspace owner. Selects the first ready, valid, conflict-free backlog task in the owner's order and, in one transaction, reserves its footprint, records an execution claim for the calling machine, moves it to `in-progress` and stores the request receipt. Answers `idle` (a receipt with no claim) when nothing is admissible. The calling machine is the session's, never a field of this input. A claim grants execution of that one attempt only; completion still needs owner approval.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: Durable unique ID for one intended admission, persisted by the caller before sending. Reuse it unchanged after any uncertainty: a retry replays the stored receipt and never admits a second task.

parameters.name: caller_version
parameters.description: The calling binary's version. It must equal the owner's.

parameters.name: caller_schema
parameters.description: The caller's distributed-drain wire-protocol schema version.

parameters.name: caller_before_pr
parameters.description: Whether the executor's drain captured `review.timing = before_pr` at submission. Diagnostic only: a claimed leaf runs the before-PR review the owner's `ship` contract captures, never the executor's own. After-landing review never affects admission.

parameters.name: caller_fingerprint
parameters.description: Type-derived pull request fingerprint negotiated with orbit.drain.probe. A mismatch is refused as protocol_skew before deserialization; optional for historical requests.

parameters.name: review_gate
parameters.description: Whether the executor's claimed PR leaf runs the before-PR review the `ship` contract captures. An owner with `review.timing = before_pr` refuses an executor that does not declare it as `before_pr_unsupported`. Omitted: `false`.

parameters.name: visual_resolution
parameters.description: Retired with visual review: accepted from an executor on an earlier build and ignored. Omit it.

parameters.name: caller_review_policy
parameters.description: Deprecated and ignored: the review-policy label distributed-drain protocol revisions before 5 sent. Accepted only so an older caller is refused as `protocol_mismatch` rather than for an unknown field.

parameters.name: run_context
parameters.description: The calling drain: `run_id`, `job_name`, and an optional diagnostic `machine_name`.

parameters.name: ship
parameters.description: The ship contract this owner resolves, exactly as `orbit.drain.probe` reported it. A new request carrying anything else is refused as `ship_contract_mismatch`, because the receipt freezes it.

parameters.name: crews
parameters.description: The crews the executor can run: `runnable` (its window preflight's crew names), `default_crew` (what a task naming no crew runs as there) and `excluded` (crews it cannot run, with why). A task whose crew it cannot run is skipped and stays in the backlog. Omitted: every crew is admissible.

parameters.name: os
parameters.description: The executor's host OS: `linux`, `macos` or `windows`. A task tagged `os:<name>` is admitted only to an executor whose OS it names, and is otherwise skipped and stays in the backlog. Omitted: only tasks without an `os:` tag are admissible.

parameters.name: browser_kit
parameters.description: Whether the executor's host has a verified headless browser kit. A task tagged `ui` is admitted only to an executor that declares one, and is otherwise skipped and stays in the backlog. Omitted: `false`.

name: orbit.task.recover
description: Operator recovery for stuck claims, blocked tasks, handoffs and reviews.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Action (required): recover_claim (claim_id, expected_phase, status, reason, request_key); requeue (id, reason); repilot (id); retry_handoff (handoff_id, expected_candidate_commit, expected_base_commit, expected_latest_attempt, expected_latest_state, reason, request_key); revoke_handoff (handoff_id, expected_candidate_commit, expected_base_commit, reason, request_key); review_reset (id, lineage_key, reason); reconcile_review (mode, id).

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: recover_claim, requeue, retry_handoff, revoke_handoff, review_reset, reconcile_review: Audit reason.

parameters.name: request_key
parameters.description: recover_claim, retry_handoff, revoke_handoff, reconcile_review: Idempotent replay key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: requeue, repilot, review_reset, reconcile_review: Task ID.

parameters.name: lineage_key
parameters.description: review_reset: Lineage key from refusal or review manifest.

parameters.name: adopt_configured_budget
parameters.description: review_reset: Adopt current limits (default keeps captured).

name: orbit.task.show
description: Fetch a task as JSON by globally unique `id`; optional `workspace` is a fail-closed filter. Use `fields` (alias `field`) for projections, or `field: "delivery"` for bounded commit/landing evidence. Projection, routing and delivery details: installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Fields (`delivery` = landing); not with claimed pagination.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: Alias for `fields`; not with claimed pagination.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: `field: "delivery"` run (default newest); not with claimed pagination.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Claimed page size; not with projections.

name: orbit.task.update
description: Update a task and return its JSON; rules are in the installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: Selects guarded update ('verdict', 'complete'; 'comment'; 'status'); omit for ordinary update.

name: orbit.workflow
description: Ship tasks, land one, or observe and control the workspace auto-drain.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: auto: Resize drain ID (omit if sole).

parameters.name: review
parameters.description: auto, ship: Review layer (`before-landing` preferred; `before-pr` deprecated).

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: auto: Stop cancel active work (default false).

name: proc.spawn
description: Spawn a process with timeout and capture output. The timeout ceiling is 60000 ms outside a managed activity; inside one it is the activity's remaining wall-clock budget, at most 45 min

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: Arguments to pass to the program

parameters.name: timeout_ms
parameters.description: Execution timeout in milliseconds (default 15000). Larger values are clamped to the effective ceiling, which the result reports as timeout_ceiling_ms: 60000 outside a managed activity, or the smaller of the activity's remaining budget and 45 min inside one
